findingsCorrected.baselineGap: The package allowed an atomic full-snapshot version guard for a late application resend but did not examine cold rebuild from a compacted recovery source.
findingsCorrected.evidence: Kafka 4.1 cleaner selects the last log offset for a key. With stable key/partition and append history v2,v3,v2, a live maximum-version sink can retain v3 while eligible compaction may remove v3 and leave the final v2 for a fresh sink.
findingsCorrected.correction: Added the retained-history counterexample, conditional nondecreasing canonical publication or an independently sufficient snapshot/checkpoint and replay boundary, preservation of delete/epoch metadata, and a check of actual retained offsets/values. Cleanup policy changes cannot restore removed records.
findingsCorrected.consequence: Avoid approving a recovery source from a successful live-sink/shuffle test alone; preserve valid live final-state convergence and adequate alternate recovery contracts.

findingsCorrected.baselineGap: The key-lane snippet used rec.key().hashCode() without declaring a key value type; byte[] uses inherited Object hashing and distinct equal-byte keys can be routed to different lanes.
findingsCorrected.evidence: JLS 17 array members inherit Object methods except clone; Arrays.hashCode(byte[]) gives equal hashes for equal contents. The executed Java negative control routed equal-byte distinct arrays to different lanes and completed the second effect first.
findingsCorrected.correction: Declared the snippet's byte[] key contract, used Arrays.hashCode(byte[]), and explained immutable value-key alternatives, stable canonicalization/mapping, mutation avoidance, and benign hash collisions sharing a lane.
findingsCorrected.consequence: The illustrative serial-lane routing now enforces equal logical key routing under its stated assumptions; it does not claim complete Kafka consumer correctness.

structuredWalkthroughs.result: v2,v3,v2 is sufficient for live atomic max-version state v3, but eligible key compaction may leave only final v2 for an empty sink. Source-backed reasoning; not a broker experiment.

Under the paired case's accepted retention and no-compaction constraints, all three records remain through rebuild; the same atomic version guard can reconstruct v3. A publication-order change is not justified solely by the compacted-history failure.
The new recovery subsection does not relax existing every-delta/intermediate-effect requirements; it is explicitly scoped to complete authoritative snapshots.
An independently sufficient accepted snapshot/checkpoint plus its replay boundary remains a valid alternative; the revision does not mandate sorting all streams.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1 design: Log Compaction Details
sources.supports: Cleaner summarizes last offset per key and removes older occurrences; compaction runs asynchronously. The v2/v3/v2 recovery counterexample is an explicit inference from this rule.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1 topic configuration: cleanup.policy
sources.supports: compact keeps latest log value per key; delete removes segments by time/size; combined policies do both.

sources.title: Java Language Specification 17, section 10.7 Array Members
sources.supports: Arrays inherit Object members except clone, including hashCode.

sources.title: Java SE 17 Arrays.hashCode(byte[])
sources.supports: Content-based hashing; equal byte-array contents produce equal hashes.

mustObserve: The response obtains compact policy from the artifact and separates live v3 convergence from empty-sink rebuild after eligible cleanup.
It identifies the last-offset v2 can survive while v3 is removed; producer idempotence and the sink guard cannot reconstruct a missing authoritative version.

It updates the proposed decision to withhold the topic-only rebuild guarantee and names a concrete sufficient repair: nondecreasing authoritative canonical publication with existing history reconciliation, or an independently sufficient authoritative snapshot/checkpoint plus replay boundary.
It retains the accepted live-snapshot contract and equal-version conflict policy, and does not impose every-intermediate transition semantics that the fixture excludes.
It does not claim compaction happens immediately, that changing cleanup.policy resurrects removed data, or that a last-value in-memory model is a Kafka execution.
observableFailures: Approves cold rebuild solely because the live sink is at v3 or the producer is idempotent.
Claims Kafka compaction retains maximum payload version.
Changes unrelated partition count or all consumers without linking the change to recovery evidence.
Reports a broker test or measured gain that was not executed.

mustObserve: The response obtains delete-only policy from the changed artifact and uses the accepted time/size window evidence to keep all listed records available through this rebuild.
It keeps the atomic version-guard and application-resend ordering decision for the specified final-state-only outcome; processing v2,v3,v2 reconstructs v3.
It scopes approval to the accepted retained history, stable mapping, full snapshots, atomic insertion/update and no required intermediate effects.
It does not require canonical publication reordering solely because the compact-policy case would need it, and does not claim deletion retention is sufficient forever.
It labels review reasoning versus unexecuted Kafka/database checks accurately.
observableFailures: Rejects this bounded rebuild for key compaction even though compact is absent.
Approves indefinitely without the accepted retention window.
Forces a sequencer or repartitioning without a remaining violated requirement.
Infers a behavioral gain from the paired walkthrough.

assumptionsAndLimitations: The counterexample assumes one stable serialized key and partition, identical payload for repeated v2, authoritative full snapshots, and deliberately skippable intermediates.

The Java correction assumes the snippet's existing non-null key, nonempty workers, stable routing, FIFO admission, one worker per lane and effect-before-return contracts. Hash collisions may reduce concurrency but do not break per-key routing.
No claim is made that these two additions exhaust all ordering defects or improve actual agent behavior.
External source content was verified for the preserved Kafka 4.1 and Java 17 reference baselines; target projects still require their actual versions/configuration.
